final.angle:
One protagonist makes one unbroken remote journey: a rainy night far from Rome, a live video viewing of a real BOOM listing on a phone in a stand, first light above the clouds, and a quiet Roman street with the keys in his hand. The legal close done from abroad is the plot. It appears as a thin system layer in BOOM's own console language: gold mono split-flap eyebrows and LEDs. That layer carries across the cuts and closes two loops on screen. The first is the far-city clock, answered by the Rome clock. The second is the one pending gold LED (KEYS · ON ARRIVAL), which turns green on the ground.

Registration is never shown as a timed event. It is the standing fact that explains "Legally." on the end card ("Your lease, registered with the Agenzia delle Entrate."). The room he watched on the phone comes back without words after the keys: the screen becomes the room.

Every BOOM interior is real: genuine walkthrough footage of the chosen listing plus its enhanced photos, moved in 2D only. The generated frames show only a foreign flat, an aircraft cabin and a zone-neutral Roman garden wall with no entrance.

This is deliberately not GPT's per-service films: no suitcase arrival, no service explainer. One man, one continuous story, with the remote legal close as the plot.

final.rationale:
WHY THIS BASE
The 'hook' treatment (best combined score) stays the spine:
- Frame 0 is already moving, calls out the right viewer and names the brief's fear in BOOM's voice.
- The promise arrives inside the first beat budget.
- A persistent console-language system layer closes on screen.
- A dark-to-dark loop brings the viewer back to the start.

It stays a different idea from GPT's per-service films: one man, one unbroken remote journey, with the legal close as the plot.

WHAT CHANGED
Two truth blockers reshaped the payoff.
1. Registration left the LED/clock mechanic entirely. A green REGISTERED LED under a landing clock tells every viewer "registered by the time you land". BOOM does not offer that: the legal deadline is 30 days and the ASPI send is manual by default. So the in-air stack is now three true rows in BOOM's real order (PAID THROUGH BOOM · RECEIPT → LEASE SIGNED ONLINE → ○ KEYS · ON ARRIVAL). Registration becomes the standing, timeless fact that explains "Legally." on the end card, in index.html's own words.
2. "Keys when you land. / This time, it's in writing." implied a written keys-on-landing guarantee, and in variant D it had BOOM repeat the scammer's line. It is now "Keys in hand. / Signed before you flew.": exactly what the film shows, working in every variant, and in D rhyming by contrast.

Three reels blockers fixed readability and platform mechanics.
- Every payoff element now holds at least 1.3 s.
- Story/Highlight became a sticker-free film segment plus a separate sticker end card (stickers can't be timed).
- The cover is a separately exported settled frame, not frame 0's random flaps.

The spot grew from 21 to 24 s (inside the brief's 18–25). The extra time went where reading needs it: the hook (3.2 s), the rhyme and a two-phase end card. A 15 s paid cutdown is delivered at zero credits.

GEOMETRY AND FAILURE MODES (AI blockers and majors)
S1 (identity anchor):
- Framing is one consistent spec: ends at mid-chest, head top at 40%.
- Readable 3:1 fill, both ears, navy that reads navy.
- The unseen phone is no longer named, so it can't leak into frame. No rain shadows are baked into the reference.
- The Kling actions now happen inside the kept trim, with no eye-darting.

S2 (screen plate):
- Behind his LEFT shoulder for lamp continuity with S1.
- 85mm at 65 cm, so a real-size phone fills 38% without becoming a tablet.
- The phone sits on the lens axis past his ear; moderate brightness, no bloom.
- Arms in his lap. A reference line forbids reproducing S1's frontal face.
- The window may show only formless reflections.

S3 (cabin):
- A physically possible cabin: right-hand window seat, camera forward on the window side, a rounded-rectangle window at the far left edge, a 30° head turn keeping both eyes, and no passenger service unit or pictograms.
- Kling moves only the clouds; no light change.

S4 (street):
- The keys are pinched and hanging, not lying across an open palm.
- The action is one breath and one blink.
- A POSITIVE doorless setting (a garden boundary wall) replaces a list of negations.
- The wall sits in open shade, so white and gold type hold.

All Kling prompts:
- Positive text of about 90 words.
- Exclusions moved to the negative field.
- Parameters set via the API.

Every on-screen claim is literally true today:

scores.strengths: Best fit for how Reels convert. Frame 0 does three jobs at once, with no fade: it is already moving (the Kling clip is trimmed to start at 0.7s, plus the split-flap), it calls out the right viewer ('RENTING IN ROME FROM ABROAD?'), and it names the fear in BOOM's own voice ('Don't send a deposit to a stranger.'). By 2.4s the answer is on screen ('See it live, on video.'), so the promise is clear well inside 3 seconds. Retention is designed in: the Tokyo clock is answered by the Rome clock, and the hollow 'KEYS · ON ARRIVAL' LED left pending in the air flips green on the ground, which gives the viewer a reason to stay. At 20s it is the shortest of the three, so completion should be highest. The loop is built dark-to-dark with a seamless seam, and the text loops answer back to question. The CTA is the strongest: DM keyword 'ROME' plus link in bio, UTM-tagged per hook. It is also the only treatment that remembers boom-track.js must be live before judging, and it offers type-only A/B hooks at zero credits. It has the lowest-risk composite: the phone sits on a stand facing the camera, with no hands and the window behind it, so a 4-corner pin is enough, followed by a push-through into the real listing photo. Claims are carefully chosen ('PAID · SECURE CHECKOUT · RECEIPT', no English-lease claim, and 'A REAL BOOM HOME' labels the real interiors).
scores.weaknesses: (1) It has the most on-screen text: eyebrow plus 84px headline on frame 0, then a headline plus a 4-line status stack in B4. That goes against the Apple-restraint brief and adds reading load for a muted viewer. (2) S1 is a weak identity anchor. The face is lit from below by the phone, with rain shadows on the cheek and the eyes lowered. S3 and S4 must copy the identity from it, so drift risk is real. (3) The Kling prompt on the hook shot asks for the light to change in brightness 2–3 times. That invites flicker on the single most important second, and the fallback (a still plus a push) loses the 'already moving' hook. (4) 'REGISTERED' appears as completed while he is still in flight, which implies a timing BOOM cannot promise for every deal; the treatment only offers a hedge. (5) Tokyo as the origin city is arbitrary for a UN/embassy/US/UK audience, and the clock depends on a DST caveat (Rome 12:40 is valid only from 25 Oct). (6) The metallic 'tink' is synced to keys that do not move on screen.

scores.strengths: The strongest emotional truth. 'Send the deposit today. Keys when you land.' is the exact scam script this audience has received, so the scroll stops on recognition. The face-down phone is a wordless sign of distrust. The payoff is the best copy in the whole set: the stranger's line comes back as BOOM's fact, without quotation marks, followed by 'This time, it's in writing.' The narrative closure pays off the watch-through. It addresses the brief's fear directly: the deposit row answers the hook ('PAID · RECEIPT ISSUED'). Trust detail is true and useful: 'You direct the camera' is on virtual-viewing.html and faq.html, 'Italian Revenue Agency' glosses the Agenzia delle Entrate for expats, and 'Egidi Immobiliare S.r.l. · licensed agency, Rome' matches index.html. Continuity is built in: the same real listing appears in the phone and in the payoff. The loop is dark-to-dark.
scores.weaknesses: (1) Misattribution risk in the first second. A muted viewer sees 'Send the deposit today.' coming from a brand account, and the attribution ('— someone you've never met') does not arrive until 1.9s. For a trust brand, that ambiguity is costly. (2) Frame 0 has little motion: a still man and a face-down phone, with motion relying on a post glow and a buzz SFX most viewers won't hear. (3) BOOM's own promise is not stated until 3.4s. (4) The post-motion phone still is a first-person POV with both hands gripping a phone held perfectly parallel. That is the hardest hand/phone generation in the set, and hands and phones are the known #1 failure point. (5) A 4.2s pure-graphics console in the middle of the spot risks a retention dip. (6) 'Deposit paid' simplifies deals where the deposit is split between signing and move-in. (7) The Kling key shot has the palm raised, so the hand is animated.

scores.strengths: The most elegant and brand-true craft. There is one type grid on every beat, Thin 100, with gold held back for the single word 'Legally.' It has the best visual rhyme: the warm real room glowing in a phone on a cold foreign night returns full-bleed in a wordless beat, so the screen has become the room. It has the best production engineering. The identity anchor is deliberately three-quarter and lamp-lit. The phone shot is landscape because the real listing photos are landscape, which gives native pins. The over-the-ear geometry makes a wrong-side phone impossible. There are no doors anywhere, and a frame-by-frame QA gate checks the key. It is the only treatment that gives an explicit truth hedge: the order of the beats shows the sequence of services, not a guaranteed registration before any particular flight. It also adds the rule to choose the listing in the marketLane now/ahead lane on publish day, and the rule that sound must not contradict picture (no key clink).
scores.weaknesses: Weakest on this lens. The hook is 'Rome.' over an interior. It is pretty, but it reads like any property ad. It doesn't qualify the viewer as someone renting from abroad until 'You're not there yet.' at 3.0s, and the actual promise (Seen live) arrives at 5.4s, so the promise isn't clear in under 3 seconds. The fear this brief exists to kill (sending a deposit to a stranger) is never named, and money or receipts never appear. The CTA is generic (URL, plus 'DM us to book a live viewing' only in the caption). The loop goes from a black end card back to a bright phone frame, so it is not seamless. At 22s with a long silent beat, completion may suffer.

scores.strengths: The strongest brand and craft piece of the three and the closest to the Apple restraint the brief asks for. It uses the fewest words: four literally true milestones (Seen live · Signed online · Registered · Keys on arrival), each on one fixed type grid, plus one silent beat. It has the best structural idea of the three: the REAL listing photo glowing in her phone in beat 1 comes back full-bleed in beat 7, so the screen becomes the room. Real BOOM product sits in frame 0, and the pull-out reveal is also the hook. The identity anchor is chosen correctly: still #1 is a sharp, three-quarter, lamp-lit face with hands still in her lap, the right reference for stills #2 to #4. The Kling beats carry the least risk of the three. The abroad shot has only breath, a blink and rain rivulets. The plane shot keeps her hands out of frame. The street shot has NO doors, no numbers and a key hanging still at her side. The signature is an abstract gold stroke made in post, never a generated hand signing. Landscape phone orientation pins BOOM's landscape listing photos natively, and the OTS camera sits on her eyeline, which rules out the wrong-side phone by geometry. It has the most complete truth audit: the lease is never claimed to be in English, and the registration timing is flagged. Every Kling beat has a zero-credit fallback, and the spend order is gated (approve #1 before spending more).
scores.weaknesses: The composite still (#2) still depends on two generated hands holding a landscape phone with thumbs on the bezel. That is the #1 failure class, and it also has to be square-on from behind her ear, which is only moderately likely in one attempt. The key at hip height in a 40mm medium-wide frame will be about 60-70 px on a 1080 master: the payoff object barely reads on a phone. Thin 100 at 104 px breaks up under Instagram compression on bright plaster and cloud-lit frames. The in-screen 'LIVE' REC chip over a drifting still photo is a small dramatization, and the claim should live in the type. The hook word 'Rome.' is beautiful but semantically weak. The line that actually hits ('You're not there yet.') only lands at 3.0s. Payment, the literal fear of the €3,000 deposit, is never named. 'Registered.' placed in flight implies the registration timing, as the treatment itself admits.

scores.strengths: It has the best composite feasibility of the three. S2 is a phone in a plain black desk stand, square to a locked-off OTS lens, with no hands, the window behind it so no glare, and a flat grey screen. It is close to a guaranteed one-shot 4-corner pin. Beat 1 also removes both failure classes: the phone and hands are out of frame and only the phone light plays on his face. It has the strongest watch-through mechanics. The hollow 'KEYS · ON ARRIVAL' LED left pending in the air flips green on the ground, the Tokyo clock is answered by the Rome clock, the real listing window match-cuts to the plane window, and the keys' glint grows into the mark before a loop to black. Craft details show real production judgment: a DST-correct clock inside BOOM's viewing window, Inter/IBM Plex Mono because the site fonts are not licensed for video, zero-credit type-only A/B hooks, cuts snapped to the trending track's beat grid, 'PAID · SECURE CHECKOUT · RECEIPT' (the deposit fear answered and true), a mono 'A REAL BOOM HOME · PRATI' label, and a prepared DM 'ROME' quick reply.
scores.weaknesses: The identity anchor is the weakest of the three. S1 is a near-black, phone-underlit face with eyes down, and it is the reference for two DAYLIGHT stills (plane and street). Underlighting distorts facial structure, so identity drift in S3/S4 is a real retry risk at 14.5 credits each. The key shot puts a walnut portone in frame, reintroducing failure class #2 (doors), and an open palm held up for 5s in Kling is a posed gesture that tends to drift. It is the least restrained: frame 0 stacks a split-flap eyebrow and a two-line headline, and the plane beat carries a headline plus four mono status rows. That is performance density, not Apple silence. The status stack over the plane implies that registration happens before landing. At 0.75s per cut, the real listing photos flash by too quickly to build trust in the home.

scores.strengths: It has the truest emotional premise. Opening on the scam script every expat has received ('Send the deposit today. Keys when you land.') over a phone turned face down stops the scroll by recognition, and the callback resolves it cleanly. The face-down phone with rear cameras up is correct physics and cannot show the wrong side. The man never touches it in the Kling shot. A post-only halo stands in for the notification. The console beat is the most explicit proof of the legal close: proposal, deposit with receipt, lease signed online, and registration with the Agenzia delle Entrate. All four are literally true, and the deposit row directly defuses the fear. The end-card micro-line 'Egidi Immobiliare S.r.l. · licensed agency, Rome' is true (index.html) and adds real trust. 'A REAL BOOM HOME · <LISTING>' honestly separates real interiors from generated frames. Using the listing's real MP4 walkthrough inside the screen when one exists is the most truthful screen content of the three. The colour-temperature arc is well judged.
scores.weaknesses: It carries the most generation risk of the three. The composite still is a first-person POV with both hands wrapping a phone perfectly parallel to the lens: visible fingers, thumbs that must stay off the glass, and a watch. It is feasible but not a one-shot certainty. The Kling beat 1 puts his hands flat on the table beside a phone and mug that must stay still, so both failure classes are in the same shot. The keys are held at chest height with sway permitted, which invites morphing. A palazzo portone behind him brings back the door risk. The first words a muted viewer reads next to the BOOM brand are 'Send the deposit today': a brand-association risk. The payoff 'Keys when you land.' repeats the scammer's words, and 'This time, it's in writing' is softer than 'Legally.' The 4.2s graphics console (headline plus four mono rows plus a subline at 28 px) is dense for a Reel and far from Apple restraint. The identity anchor has his eyes lowered to the table, a weaker reference for the daylight stills.

This removes the #1 failure class from the one frame that has to be pixel-exact for the corner-pin.

Let the end card dim to pure black in the last 0.5s so the Reel loops into the dark frame 0 without a visible seam. issues.problem: The S3 camera geometry cannot work. The camera sits 'from the empty middle seat beside him', which is the aisle side. The window is on his other side, so it lands BEHIND his head, not at 'frame left-centre'. If he turns '45 degrees toward the window', his face turns AWAY from the lens, and the dawn light hits the cheek we cannot see. The model has to break the cabin to satisfy all three constraints: a window floating on the camera side, rows facing the wrong way, or the back of his head. This is exactly the aircraft-geometry botch the brief warned about.
issues.fix: Replace the camera paragraph: 'He sits in a window seat on the right-hand side of the aircraft, so the window is on his right. Camera: at his seated eye level, just forward of him on the window side, as if from the window seat of the row ahead with that seat removed, looking back at him about 35 degrees off his nose line; true 50mm, f/2. The window is at the far left edge of the frame, seen at an angle. He turns his head about 30 degrees toward it, toward frame left and just past the lens. We see his face in three-quarter view with both eyes visible, lit on the camera side by the window light.' Delete 'from the empty middle seat beside him' and 'face turned about 45 degrees toward the window at frame left'. Beat 3's match cut then uses a real window placed at the left edge (±10%).

issues.problem: The cabin will show a bad window and generated text. 'One oval cabin window' produces a porthole or ellipse, which reads as fake; real airliner windows are rounded rectangles in a thick sidewall bezel. 'The dim curve of the cabin ceiling and a closed overhead bin' invites the passenger service unit, whose reading lights, vents and seat-belt or no-smoking icons are generated pictograms or text. Banning only 'signs' does not stop that unit from appearing. A low sun in the window also risks a clipped sun disc.
issues.fix: Use: 'a single standard airliner cabin window: a rounded-rectangle opening about 25 cm wide and 35 cm tall, set in a thick, pale, curved plastic sidewall bezel, with the pull-down shade raised so only its thin edge shows at the top. The sun itself is outside the window's view; only its warm light enters. Above him there is only the smooth, unlit curve of the sidewall and the underside of the overhead bin, falling into deep shadow. No passenger service unit, vents, reading lights, call buttons or icons are in frame.'

issues.problem: The S3 motion prompt breaks the treatment's own rule that no light change is asked of Kling. It asks the band of dawn light to 'brighten gradually and slide about two centimetres toward his ear'. Kling renders this as exposure pumping or flicker on the face, and it can drag the skin texture with the light. It also asks for clouds 'right to left', which no longer matches the corrected geometry.
issues.fix: Delete the light-band sentence. Add: 'The light on his face stays exactly as it is, with the same brightness, the same position and no flicker. Only the clouds outside the window move, slowly and steadily, toward the rear of the aircraft, staying inside the window opening.' Keep the blink at about 1.5 s and the closed-mouth smile from about 2.5 s.

issues.problem: The S4 hand pose exposes the most failure-prone anatomy. It asks for an open palm turned up at chest height with 'fingers gently curled' and two keys 'lying across his fingers'. All five fingers are visible and foreshortened toward the camera, and keys lying on fingers merge with them, so finger counts and fused keys are likely. 'Five natural fingers, anatomically correct' does not prevent this. A palm-up hand held out while he looks at the windows also reads as a staged key presentation.
issues.fix: Replace it with: 'His right hand is raised to upper-chest height, close to his body. He holds a plain steel key ring pinched between his thumb and the side of his bent index finger; his other three fingers are loosely curled into his palm. Exactly two plain brass keys hang straight down from the ring, side by side and slightly fanned so they do not overlap, clearly visible against the navy sweater, with one small warm highlight on the brass.' Then update the composition line to 'keys at about 60 percent of frame height'.

issues.problem: The S4 Kling motion puts too many actions on details that are too small. At mid-thigh framing his face is about 220 px wide on the 1080 output, and the key cluster is roughly 70 to 95 px. At that scale Kling 3.0 morphs faces and small metal objects. The prompt still asks for a gaze lift, an exhale, a widening smile, a blink and a 5 cm push, and every extra facial action adds morph risk to a face that is barely readable. The QA gate will probably fail, which wastes the most expensive credit of the spot.
issues.fix: Rewrite the action part: 'Camera: one very slow push-in of about 3 centimetres at eye level, with a constant 50mm focal length. He stays completely still except for one slow breath at about 2 seconds (his shoulders rise and settle) and one natural blink at about 3.5 seconds. His gaze and expression do not change. His right hand, every finger, the ring and the two keys do not move at all.' Move all 'no ...' items to the negative-prompt field (see the Kling negative-prompt issue). Keep the frame-by-frame QA check on the keys.

issues.problem: The street asks for 'no doorways ... anywhere' through negation, while also describing a 'narrow residential street' of Roman facades that recedes behind him. Street-level portoni, intercoms, house numbers and shopfronts are the defining feature of such a street. The model will add them, especially in the receding background, which brings back both the door problem and generated numbers or text. The Avoid list names eight lettering-bearing objects (doorbells, nameplates, intercoms, licence plates and so on), which primes them.
issues.fix: Give the model a positive, doorless setting instead: 'He stands in front of a long, plain, sun-warmed ochre plaster boundary wall of a Roman palazzo garden, about 3 metres behind him, with a trail of ivy spilling over its top. Above and beyond it, softly out of focus, are the upper floors of ochre and terracotta facades with closed dark-green shutters and small iron balconies. Grey basalt sampietrini at his feet. At ground level behind him there is only this continuous wall.' Cut the Avoid list to: 'no people, vehicles, doorways, signs, numbers or lettering of any kind.'

issues.problem: S1's framing contradicts itself, and the arms sentence is physically impossible. First, it says 'Medium close-up from mid-chest to a little above the top of his head' but also 'top of head at about 40 percent, upper 38 percent empty'. Second, 'forearms rest on the edge of the desk and angle down and out of the bottom of the frame': forearms resting on a desk are horizontal, and at mid-chest framing the desk is below the frame, so the model may invent visible arms or hands. Third, 'keep his head and shoulders clear of the right 12 percent' is impossible, because a centred medium close-up this tight is about 48 cm wide and his shoulders fill it. The right-rail rule applies to type, not to the picture.
issues.fix: Replace these with: 'Medium close-up: the frame ends at mid-chest, above the desk surface; his arms and hands are entirely below the frame edge. Generous headroom: the top of his head is at 40 percent of frame height, and everything above it is empty, softly lit dark wall.' Delete the forearm sentence, 'to a little above the top of his head', and the 'clear of the right 12 percent' sentence.

issues.problem: S1 names a 'smartphone ... in a small desk stand just below the bottom edge of the frame'. Mentioning an object in order to hide it is a classic failure: the top of a phone, or a phone in his hand, often appears at the bottom edge. It may be the wrong side, with the back camera toward us, which is the exact error the GPT pipeline paid to fix. This is the identity anchor, and a reroll here is expensive.
issues.fix: Delete the smartphone sentence. Use: 'He is reading something on the desk just below the frame edge; a faint cool-neutral glow rises from there onto his chin and lower eyelids.' Keep 'no phone, screen or glowing object in frame' in Avoid.

issues.problem: S1 is a weak identity reference for three stills. The key light falls off 'into shadow on frame left' in a near-black frame, so half the face (jaw contour, cheek, ear) is guessed differently in each derived still. The navy sweater under dim 2700K light will render near-black, so S3 and S4 will drift toward black or royal blue. The 'raindrop shadows' on the sweater get baked into the reference, and derived stills tend to copy them as spots or stains on the knit. S2 relies on 'ear shape', but here the ears are soft and partly hidden.
issues.fix: Add: 'Key-to-fill ratio about 3:1: the shadow side of his face stays readable, with skin tone and the cheek and jaw contour visible, never crushed to black. Both ears are visible. The sweater reads clearly as deep navy, not black.' Delete the raindrop-shadow sentence from S1, and from the S1 motion prompt. If rain shadows are wanted, add them as a masked overlay in post, as the fallback already plans.

issues.problem: The S1 motion timing does not match the edit. The brow lift and exhale are timed at 3.5 s, but the clip is trimmed to 0.7–3.1 s, so the only facial event that survives is the blink at 2 s. Credits go on motion that is cut. The 'small left-to-right reading movements' of the eyes are a known Kling failure: darting, twitchy or rolling eyes on the most-watched second of the Reel. The 'raindrop shadows drift downward' over merino makes the knit texture swim.
issues.fix: Rewrite the action block: 'He stays seated, looking down at something just below the frame; his gaze stays steady, with no darting eye movements. At about 1.2 seconds he blinks once, naturally. At about 2.2 seconds his brows lift very slightly and he exhales once, softly, through his nose; his shoulders settle a few millimetres.' Delete the raindrop sentence and the reading-movement sentence. Change the trim to 0.6–3.0 s.

issues.problem: S2's optics are inconsistent. A true 50mm lens on a camera behind his shoulder, about 65–70 cm from the phone, frames about 34 cm horizontally, so a 7 cm phone screen fills about 21 percent of the width, not the 38 percent the prompt asks for. To hit 38 percent at 50mm the camera would have to sit about 38 cm from the phone, which is in front of his face. The model will either shrink the phone, make it tablet-sized, or bend perspective, and the plate gets worse for the composite and the 265% push.
issues.fix: Change the camera line to: 'Locked-off camera about 65 centimetres from the phone, just behind and above his right shoulder, looking down at about 20 degrees; true 85mm perspective, f/5.6.' At 85mm and 0.65 m the frame is about 18 cm wide, so a 7 cm screen fills about 38 percent, which matches the spec. At this aperture the focus plane on the screen is only a few centimetres deep: the screen stays sharp while the shoulder and the window blur heavily.

issues.problem: Three failure modes for the composite. First, the camera sits behind his RIGHT shoulder while the phone is centred in front of HIM, so the lens sees the screen about 15–20° off-axis. Demanding 'exactly perpendicular, no keystone' pushes the model toward a flat, pasted-on phone. Second, a lamp 'beside the desk, level with the phone' in front of a black night window will reflect in the window glass, and possibly show his face reflected, which creates identity chaos. 'It cannot reflect in the glass' is a wish, not geometry. The lamp may also appear in frame, and 'upper 30% no bright light' conflicts with 'city bokeh lights'. Third, a lit screen in a dark room is often rendered blown out, with a bloom halo over the bezel, which ruins the corner pin. His arms are also never placed, so the model may put hands or forearms on the desk next to the stand.
issues.fix: Add: 'The phone stands slightly to the right of his centreline, directly on the camera's line of sight past his right ear, so the screen faces the lens. A slight natural perspective is acceptable; all four rounded corners must be visible, crisp and unoccluded. Screen brightness is moderate, not blown out; the bezel edge is crisp with no bloom or halo. His arms rest in his lap below the desk edge; no forearm, hand or finger is anywhere on the desk. The only other light is a dim warm lamp out of frame, behind the camera on the left. The dark window glass shows only faint, formless, defocused reflections, never a readable reflection of him, the lamp or the phone. Beyond the glass are a few small, dim, defocused city lights, none brighter than the screen.' Replace 'like an 18 percent grey card' with 'a uniform neutral mid-grey with no markings'. Composite with a 4-corner pin, which handles any residual keystone.

issues.problem: S1 is supplied as an image reference with a frontal, lamp-lit face. The model tends to reproduce that face, turning him toward the lens or putting his profile and beard in frame, which violates 'his face is not visible' and competes with the screen. 'Preserve the exact same man: skin tone, hairline and ear shape' makes this worse, because it asks for facial features the shot must not show.
issues.fix: Change the reference line to: 'Use the supplied photograph only for his clothing, his skin tone at the neck and ear, the desk, the lamp colour and the room's night atmosphere. New camera position: we see him from behind. We never see his face; only the back of his neck, the rim of his right ear and his right shoulder appear, dark and out of focus in the bottom-left corner.'

issues.problem: Identity drift and style bleed affect S3 and S4 (and S2 for lighting). Two things pull against each other. The reference image transfers S1's low-key 2700K lamp grade and near-black background into the dawn cabin and the Roman morning. The prompts also re-send the full original text spec ('East African descent ... slim straight nose, full lips ... 1.82 m'). If the approved S1 differs from that text at all (hair length, beard line, collar), the model is pulled between two targets and produces a third face.
issues.fix: Open S3 and S4 with: 'Use the supplied photograph only for this man's face, hair, beard, skin tone and clothing. Do not copy its framing, lighting, colour grade or setting.' After S1 is approved, rewrite the person paragraph to describe S1 as it was rendered, or cut it to: 'the same man as in the supplied photograph, unchanged face, beard and hairline, in the same deep navy merino crew-neck with the thin white T-shirt edge at the collar.' Do not re-send spec text that the approved S1 contradicts.

issues.problem: All three Kling prompts put long 'no ...' lists into the positive prompt, for example 'no doors, no people, vehicles or birds appearing', 'no head turn toward the camera', 'no speaking' and 'no lights turning on or off'. Kling picks up nouns and verbs much more readily than gpt_image does, so naming birds, doors, speaking or head-turns raises the chance of those events. The prompts are also over 150 words and start with parameter headers ('Kling 3.0 image-to-video from S4, mode pro (1080p)...'), which dilutes adherence. This applies to beats 1, 4 and 5.
issues.fix: Set the mode, duration, ratio and sound through the API parameters, not the prompt text. Keep each positive prompt under about 90 words: 'Preserve this exact photograph...' plus the camera move plus 2–3 timed actions. Put the exclusions in Kling's negative_prompt field, e.g. 'morphing, warping, face distortion, extra fingers, extra or merging keys, text, logos, watermark, new people, doors, flicker, exposure change, camera shake, cut'.

issues.problem: The still prompts carry production metadata and a brand name into the image model: 'STILL S1 of 4, THE IDENTITY ANCHOR (gpt_image_2_5...)', 'Generate and approve this frame before any other spend', 'cinema frame for BOOM', 'this frame will be animated only in post, and its screen will be replaced'. The word BOOM and the labels are exactly what leaks as generated lettering, signage or watermarks, which the hard rules forbid. This applies to all four stills.
issues.fix: Strip every header and production note from the text actually sent. Start S1 with: 'One exceptionally credible cinema frame for a service that helps people rent a home in Rome legally from abroad.' Never write the brand name in a generation prompt, and keep the gating notes in the run sheet.

issues.problem: The timeline is implausible. S3 shows dawn in 'the last hour' of the flight, and S4 puts him on a Roman street holding keys at 'ROME · 09:12' / 'about 9 am'. Sunrise in Rome in October is about 07:15–07:30, so landing, passport control, baggage and the transfer from FCO leave no time for a 09:12 key handover. It is small, but the on-screen clock invites the arithmetic.
issues.fix: Change the eyebrow to 'ROME · 10:40' and S4's light to 'mid-morning, low autumn sun raking along the wall'. Alternatively drop the minutes and use 'ROME · MORNING'.

issues.problem: The type contradicts the treatment's own rule of never more than three text elements on screen at once. At 9.05 s the screen shows the headline, four stack rows and a gloss line. At 12.1 s it shows the eyebrow, rows 3–4 and the gloss. The gloss 'Italian Revenue Agency' at 20 px in #8A8A90 over a dark cabin will not survive Instagram compression.
issues.fix: Treat the stack as one element and say so in the rule. Raise the gloss to Inter 300, 22 px, #B0B0B6, or merge it into the row as '○ REGISTERED · ITALIAN REVENUE AGENCY' and move 'Agenzia delle Entrate' to the caption.

issues.problem: The callback 'Keys when you land. / This time, it's in writing.' is ambiguous about what is in writing. It can read as 'the keys-on-arrival promise is a contract clause', which is not literally true: the keys are handed over with the verbale di consegna, and that is not a lease term.
issues.fix: Use 'This time, the lease is in writing.' or 'This time, there's a signed lease.'

issues.problem: The fallback for the on-screen content uses two still photos with a '0.5 px handheld micro-jitter so it reads as a live walk'. That fakes live footage from stills on the very beat that claims 'See it live, on video', which is a small but real honesty gap.
issues.fix: Use jitter only when the source is the listing's genuinely filmed walkthrough. With stills, use a clean 2D slide or dissolve, with no simulated handheld movement.

issues.problem: The crop rule prefers a native 9:16 crop. Real enhanced interior photos are mostly 4:3 landscape, and a 9:16 crop keeps only about 42% of their width, usually a slice of wall or a corner instead of a readable room. That undercuts the proof beat and the rhyme in beat 6. This applies to beats 3 and 6.
issues.fix: Make the 4:5 plate on #060607 the default for landscape sources. Allow full-bleed 9:16 only for photos that were shot in portrait, or where a 9:16 crop still contains a recognisable room (sofa plus window, or bed plus window).

issues.problem: The generated ochre-palazzo street, followed by the full-bleed real living room in beat 6, implies that this is the building of the chosen listing. If the listing is Bilocale Ponte Milvio (mixed or modern stock), the implied exterior misrepresents a real BOOM property.
issues.fix: Pick the listing whose real surroundings match an ochre historic street (Prati or Pigneto) and name that zone in beat 3. If Ponte Milvio is chosen, make S4's backdrop a neutral wall with no period architecture.

issues.problem: REGISTERED turns green at 12.1 s, right under the 'ROME · 09:12' clock and a beat after KEYS goes pending. Every viewer will read that as 'your lease is registered with the Agenzia delle Entrate by the time you land.' BOOM does not offer that. The ASPI send is manual by default (api/fiscal/_aspi.js has auto:false). The legal deadline is 30 days from the earlier of signing and lease start. BOOM's own pages promise 'registered within 30 days' (virtual-viewing.html), not 'registered on arrival'. The treatment's note that 'the order is what BOOM does, not a guaranteed date' never reaches the screen. It also contradicts the treatment's own rule that registration is 'never shown as completed'.
issues.fix: Take REGISTERED out of the LED/clock mechanic altogether. In-air stack (beat 4): '● PAID THROUGH BOOM · RECEIPT' / '● LEASE SIGNED ONLINE' / '○ KEYS · ON ARRIVAL'. Ground (beat 5): 'ROME · 09:12' plus 'KEYS · IN HAND' only. Registration moves to the end card as a standing, timeless fact that explains 'Legally.' Under 'Legally.' add a subline in Inter 300 30 px #C9C9CE, two lines, centred: 'Your lease, registered with the / Agenzia delle Entrate.' The claim matches index.html ('Every contract is registered with the Agenzia delle Entrate') without attaching a time to it. Delete the gloss rows at y 612/636 in beats 4 and 5.

issues.problem: 'Keys when you land. / This time, it's in writing.' tells the viewer that a keys-on-landing guarantee is written down. The lease states a start date, not a key time. /executive only says a tenancy 'can close before you land — keys on arrival day'. There is also a brand risk: in variant D, BOOM repeats word for word the line it has just attributed to a scammer. A screenshot of beat 5 on its own shows BOOM making the scammer's promise.
issues.fix: HEADLINE: 'Keys in hand.' (with 'hand.' in #FFD700). SUBLINE: 'Signed before you flew.' Both are literally what the spot has shown, and neither implies a guarantee. Variant D still rhymes by contrast: the stranger's '“Send the deposit today.” / “Keys when you land.”' against BOOM's 'Signed before you flew.' If the rhyme has to stay, use only this: '“Keys when you land.” / This time, with a signed lease behind it.' Never use 'it's in writing'.

issues.problem: The S2 prompt contradicts itself on geometry, and this is exactly the failure (phones and hands) that the pipeline cannot reroll. 'Camera just behind and slightly above his right shoulder' puts his right shoulder at frame RIGHT, but the prompt places 'his right shoulder… right ear' in the bottom-LEFT corner. Continuity also demands the LEFT side: in S1 the lamp is camera-right, which is his left, and in the reverse the prompt correctly puts the lamp 'at the far left', lighting 'the edge of his ear'. That is his left ear. There is a second risk: with S1 as the image reference, gpt_image tends to copy S1's face-to-camera composition.
issues.fix: Replace these fragments. First: 'A locked-off camera sits just behind and slightly above his LEFT shoulder, looking past him down at the desk at about 20 degrees.' Second: 'Foreground: his left shoulder, the back of his neck and the rim of his left ear fill the bottom-left corner, dark navy, soft and out of focus; the lamp at far left rims that ear with warm light.' Add a lead sentence right after the identity line: 'The supplied photograph is only an identity, wardrobe and room reference. Do NOT reproduce its camera position or framing: this is the reverse angle, from behind him, and his face is not visible.'

issues.problem: The spot's central claim, 'See it live, on video.', is illustrated with still listing photos and a fake '0.5 px handheld micro-jitter so it reads as a live walk'. This does not break the no-generated-interior rule, but it fakes liveness under a liveness claim. A zero-cost truthful option exists.
issues.fix: Put genuinely filmed footage of the chosen listing inside the screen. First choice: the operator shoots an 8–10 s vertical iPhone walk-through at 1080×1920 on publish week (corridor to living room, eye level, slow). Second choice: a screen recording of a real BOOM video viewing, cropped to picture only, with no client face or voice. Stills are a last resort: then 2D drift only and NO simulated handheld jitter. Rewrite the note: 'Never add fake camera shake to stills to imply a live call.'

issues.problem: S4's generated street is a narrow ochre and terracotta lane with sampietrini cobbles. That is Trastevere/Monti/Centro. The film labels the home 'PRATI' (or Ponte Milvio/Pigneto), then rhymes the street into that listing's real living room (beat 6). The sequence therefore presents a generated neighbourhood as the setting of a real BOOM listing, and gets the zone wrong: Prati is wide Umbertine blocks on asphalt. A viewer who later visits sees the mismatch. There is also an ordering problem: S4 is generated now, but the listing is picked 'on publish day'.
issues.fix: Choose the listing BEFORE generating S4, and write the street to match its zone. Prati: 'a quiet residential street of late-1800s Umbertine palazzi in pale cream and travertine grey, tall shuttered windows, plane-tree shade, smooth asphalt with a stone kerb, no cobbles'. Pigneto: 'low 1930s–1950s palazzine in faded ochre and pink plaster, simple balconies, asphalt'. Keep the ochre-and-cobbles lane only if the chosen listing is in Trastevere, Monti or Centro Storico. Alternatively, drop the zone from the beat-3 label.

issues.problem: The listing candidates are unverified, and the repo snapshots contradict each other. index.html's CASE data marks Bilocale Ponte Milvio (ttvrjazww9oe4tA0wHTf) 'rented' and Trilocale Pigneto 'reserved'; apartments.html shows both 'Available now'. The only Prati card is 'Free from 1 Mar 2027' (PreOrder), which means occupied. A flat in the 'ahead' lane has a sitting tenant, so 'DM “ROME” to book a live viewing' of 'that flat' may not be honoured without the tenant's consent. Also, this spot will be pinned as the main Highlight, so any named listing goes stale once it is let.
issues.fix: Rewrite post note (4): 'Pick the listing from the LIVE portal (Listings → 📅 Disponibilità), never from the HTML build snapshots, and ONLY from marketLane now. Do not use ahead: those homes are occupied. Lock it before S4 is generated.' For the Highlight master, change the beat-3 label to 'A REAL BOOM LISTING' with no zone, and diary a re-cut of the beat-2/3/6 photos when the flat is let.

issues.problem: Type density and legibility contradict the treatment's own rule of 'never more than three text elements on screen at once'. From 9.05 to 11.4 s beat 4 shows the headline, four status rows and a gloss (six elements), leaving about 2.3 s to read them. Beat 5 shows four; the end card shows six. The sizes are also too small once scaled to a phone (factor about 0.36 to points). Rows at 26 px come out around 9 pt; the gloss at 20 px around 7 pt; the legal line at 18 px in #6B6B70 on #060607 is about 6.5 pt at roughly 3.7:1 contrast. That is unreadable, and the legal line is the trust anchor.
issues.fix: Beat 4: the headline 'Before you land.' holds 7.5–8.3 s, then fades out before the stack starts. The stack has at most three rows (see the blocker fix), in IBM Plex Mono at 34 px with 60 px row pitch (baselines y 520 / 580 / 640), and no gloss in the air. End card, Reel master: mark, headline, 'Legally.', registration subline and URL. Move the 'DM “ROME”…' CTA into the caption and pinned comment. Legal line at 24 px #9A9AA0, baseline y 1420.

issues.problem: 'Egidi Immobiliare S.r.l. · licensed agency, Rome' uses an adjective the viewer cannot verify. Italian agencies are registered (REA / Chamber of Commerce), not licensed in a way a foreigner can check. The site already publishes the verifiable ID (faq.html: P.IVA 17322991005, REA RM-1710623). A checkable number beats an adjective in a spot about not trusting strangers.
issues.fix: Replace the line with: 'Egidi Immobiliare S.r.l. · REA RM-1710623 · Rome' (Inter 300, 24 px, #9A9AA0).

issues.problem: The payment row does not answer the hook. The film opens with 'Don't send a deposit to a stranger' and then shows him paying online. 'PAID · SECURE CHECKOUT · RECEIPT' does not say who received the money, so 'stranger' goes unanswered until the tiny legal line. The row order is also inaccurate: in BOOM's flow the proposal is accepted, then paid via Stripe, then the lease is signed via Magic Sign. 'SIGNED ONLINE' above 'PAID' blurs this.
issues.fix: Rows, in this order: '● PAID THROUGH BOOM · RECEIPT' / '● LEASE SIGNED ONLINE' / '○ KEYS · ON ARRIVAL'. 'THROUGH' rather than 'TO' is deliberate: BOOM is the agency, and rent and deposits are the owners' money. It also avoids naming Stripe, which is a third-party brand.

issues.problem: 'A REAL BOOM HOME' could be read as BOOM owning or operating the flat. CLAUDE.md is explicit that BOOM is only an agency and does not sublet. The site does use the phrase 'BOOM homes', but in a spot built on literal truth the precise word costs nothing.
issues.fix: Label: 'A REAL BOOM LISTING · <ZONE>'. On the Highlight master: 'A REAL BOOM LISTING'.

issues.problem: The compositing note asks for 'a 4% Screen-mode reflection made from blurred, flipped window bokeh'. That is physically wrong: the screen faces the camera and away from the window, so it cannot reflect the window behind it. A wrong reflection is exactly the detail that makes a composite read as fake.
issues.fix: Replace it with: 'a 3% Screen-mode reflection of what is BEHIND the camera: a soft warm smear on the lamp side (frame left) and the dark, defocused silhouette of his head and left shoulder. Never the window.'

issues.problem: S1's framing instruction contradicts itself, on the frame that gates the whole budget. 'Medium close-up from mid-chest to a little above the top of his head' means almost no headroom. The same prompt also asks for the top of his head at 40% and an empty upper 38% reserved for type. The model will satisfy one instruction or the other; if it picks the MCU, beat 1's headline has nowhere to sit.
issues.fix: Replace the line with: 'Medium shot from just below the chest, with deliberately generous headroom: the top of his head sits at 40 percent of frame height, eyes at 54 percent, and everything above his head is the dark, out-of-focus wall.'

issues.problem: S4's framing conflicts with itself. 'Medium shot from mid-thigh up' cannot put 'quiet trousers and cobbles' in the bottom 20%, because the ground is out of frame at mid-thigh.
issues.fix: Either say 'Medium-wide shot from just below the knees; the bottom 20 percent is trousers and street surface', or keep mid-thigh and write 'the bottom 20 percent is quiet charcoal trousers, no ground visible'. Match the street-surface wording to the zone fix.

issues.problem: S3's geometry risks showing the back of his head. From the middle seat, a passenger who turns 45° toward his own window turns away from the camera. The Kling prompt also asks the light band to 'brighten gradually and slide 2 cm', a light change that invites flicker. The treatment banned light changes on beat 1 for exactly that reason.
issues.fix: S3: 'The window sits slightly forward of his shoulder at frame left; he turns his head only about 30 degrees toward it, so the camera still sees both eyes, the near cheek and the beard line inside the gold band.' Kling: 'The band of dawn light on his face stays constant in position and brightness; only the clouds outside move.'

issues.problem: 'See it live, on video.' is slightly clumsy, and the comma splice weakens the gold emphasis on 'live'.
issues.fix: HEADLINE: 'See it live.' ('live.' in #FFD700). SUBLINE: 'On video. You direct the camera.' Both are true per index.html and faq.html.

issues.problem: The audio plan assumes trending Instagram audio. Business and brand accounts cannot use most commercial trending tracks in Reels, and paid Meta ads cannot use them at all. The edit is supposed to be locked to that track's beat grid.
issues.fix: Choose the track from Meta Sound Collection or a royalty-free licence BEFORE locking the beat-3 cuts. Master (b), with the SFX stem, is the default for the paid cut.

issues.problem: The link sticker and bio URL are not specified. CLAUDE.md records a failure (8 Sep 2026) where an apex-domain URL returned 'Redirecting...' to a crawler. UTM measurement also depends on the landing URL being exact.
issues.fix: The sticker and bio link must be 'https://www.boomrome.com/<page>?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=story&utm_campaign=lancio-2026-10&utm_content=before-you-land-A', always www. The on-screen 'BOOMROME.COM' is display text only.

issues.problem: The paid Meta cut is aimed at expats, including North America. Real-estate rental ads shown to US or Canada audiences must run under Meta's Housing Special Ad Category, which restricts age, gender and postcode targeting. Missing it gets the ad rejected or the account restricted.
issues.fix: Add to the post notes: 'Paid master: declare Special Ad Category = Housing whenever the audience includes US/CA; no demographic targeting.'

issues.problem: The logline says '9,000 km'. Tokyo to Rome is about 9,850 km. If the logline is reused in the caption or post copy, the number is wrong.
issues.fix: In any public copy, write 'almost 10,000 km from Rome' or drop the distance.

issues.problem: The payoff beat is unreadable at mobile speed. The loops the spot sets up close on screen for too short a time to read.
